items.body:
## Summary

MFSDP v2 can combine up to four microbatch gradients into one inner reduce-scatter and let autograd accumulate into the retained input buffer.

## Implementation

- Compile a fixed, rank-agreed reduction plan from the per-module gradient-ready events of one eager iteration. The opt-in `--megatron-fsdp-rs-window-budget-mib` flag caps the planned window inputs, casts, and scratch. Windows flush at the existing outer reduction boundaries.
- Bind gradient views for eligible autograd leaves on the buffer's write stream. Fall back to the existing packing path when a view cannot be used.

items.title: [Fix] kernels/lora: Use int64 token row offsets in the csgmv shrink and expand kernels
items.author: xiaoke12345678
items.summary: The chunked-SGMV (csgmv) LoRA kernels load each token's physical row from the int32 and multiply it by the row stride: / in the shrink kernel (plain and split-K) and in the expand kernel. When the int32 product wraps, so the kernels read (shrink) and read/writ…
items.body:
## Motivation

Fixes #51099.

The chunked-SGMV (csgmv) LoRA kernels load each token's physical row from the int32 `permutation` and multiply it by the row stride: `s_offset_physical * x_stride_0` / `* output_stride_0` in the shrink kernel (plain and split-K) and `* output_stride_0` in the expand kernel. When `row * stride >= 2^31` the int32 product wraps, so the kernels read (shrink) and read/write (expand) before the tensors. The Triton LoRA backend already widens the same index to int64 in `kernel_utils.py`. One forward of about `2^31 / K` tokens reaches this, e.g. a long unchunked prefill.

items.title: [Bugfix][Mamba] Default the Mamba ssm state cache to float32
items.author: sniper35
items.summary: Changes default Mamba SSM state cache dtype from bfloat16 to float32, eliminating decode-prefill log-prob drift caused by per-token rounding accumulation.
items.body:
## Overview

With `--mamba-cache-dtype` and `--mamba-ssm-cache-dtype` both on `auto`, Mamba layers keep their ssm state in the model dtype, which is bfloat16 for most checkpoints. Decode rounds the state to that dtype on every token, so the log-probs it reports drift from the ones the same engine computes when it prefills the same tokens, and the drift grows with the sequence. This PR makes float32 the default for the ssm state of Mamba layers, the default NemotronH already gets per architecture (#39032, #63218).

Fixes #68338.

items.title: [Fix] kernels/quantization: Use int64 row offsets in the int8 quant kernels
items.author: xiaoke12345678
items.summary: computed and from an int32, and did the same with. For inputs with at least 2^31 elements the product wraps to a negative offset and the kernels read and write before the tensors.
items.body:
## Motivation

Fixes #51104.

`_per_token_quant_int8` computed `row_id * stride_x` and `row_id * stride_xq` from an int32 `tl.program_id(0)`, and `_per_token_group_quant_int8` did the same with `g_id * y_stride`. For inputs with at least 2^31 elements the product wraps to a negative offset and the kernels read and write before the tensors. The fp8 siblings already use `tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64)` for this case. Activation quantization of W8A8-INT8 linear layers and the channel-wise int8 fused MoE reach this path.

## Modifications

- `kernels/ops/quantization/int8_kernel.py`: widen `row_id`

`_vit_fp8_asm_segment` quantizes q/k/v for the padded-head fp8 assembly FMHA. For each

items.title: [Feature Request]Support FP32 bias gradient accumulation in native fused Linear backward
items.author: zjjott
items.summary: Please describe. When, native can accumulate weight gradients directly into FP32, but its bias gradient still passes through BF16 before reaching the FP32 DDP buffer. With BF16, this returns a BF16 result.
items.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

When `gradient_accumulation_fusion=True`, native `LinearWithGradAccumulationAndAsyncCommunication` can accumulate weight gradients directly into FP32 `main_grad`, but its bias gradient still passes through BF16 before reaching the FP32 DDP buffer.

The relevant code is [`grad_bias = grad_output.sum(dim=0)` in layers.py](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/dev/megatron/core/tensor_parallel/layers.py#L962). With BF16 `grad_output`, this returns a BF16 result. Subsequent FP32 accumulation cannot recover the lost precision.

## Description

**Issue.** With `kv_cache_config.disk_prefetch_num_reqs > 0` a worker dies in its event loop with

`manager.shared_from_this()`. The nanobind binding takes the manager by reference, so the first
prefetch of a fresh manager, when no live `KvCache` owns it yet, throws `std::bad_weak_ptr`.

**Fix.** Bind `prefetch_reuse` by `std::shared_ptr<kv::KvCacheManager>`, like `create_kv_cache`.
One file, `cpp/tensorrt_llm/nanobind/batch_manager/kvCacheManagerV2.cpp`, +5 / -2.

items.body:
## Motivation

`response_format` (`json_schema` / `json_object`) misbehaves for Muse Glimmer and Muse Spark Open. A Muse turn is a sequence of messages: reasoning (`to=self`), optional visible commentary (`to=commentary`), tool calls (`to=<tool>`), and the answer (`<|start|>assistant to=user<|message|>…`). The JSON grammar started at the end of the first reasoning message, before the answer header. So the model either padded whitespace until `max_tokens` or wrote its next header into the JSON. items.title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Pass image kwargs through the OpenCUA processor
items.author: subhashpolisetti
items.summary: The OpenCUA image processor silently dropped sizing kwargs (max_pixels, min_pixels, size), causing unbounded image token counts; this routes them through and disables device normalization.
items.body:
## Overview

`OpenCUAProcessor.__call__` calls the image processor without any kwargs, so `min_pixels`, `max_pixels` and `size` from `--mm-processor-kwargs` or a request are silently ignored. Profiling uses the shared Qwen2-VL sizing, which does apply them. With `max_pixels=512**2` the profiled budget is 334 tokens per image, while a 1920x1080 image still produces 2,691.

items.author: ShangmingCai
items.summary: Today a PD decode server never runs a prefill forward: every request arrives through a prefill server, a bootstrap handshake and a KV transfer, even when the decode server's radix cache already holds almost the whole prompt. In multi-turn and agentic traffic t…
items.body:
## Motivation

Today a PD decode server never runs a prefill forward: every request arrives through a prefill server, a bootstrap handshake and a KV transfer, even when the decode server's radix cache already holds almost the whole prompt. In multi-turn and agentic traffic that is the common case: the decode server that served turn N holds turn N's prompt and output, so turn N+1 needs only a short prefill, and the fixed PD cost dominates its TTFT.

This PR lets a decode server prefill such requests itself, in the same running batch as its PD requests, and lets `sgl-router` decide when to send

## Motivation

With `ignore_eos`, the scheduler keeps decoding past every stop token and the response never says where the reply would have ended. A client that wants the valid prefix of a fixed-length generation has to rebuild the stop set itself (EOS, the tokenizer's additional stop tokens, `stop_token_ids`), and that copy can drift from what the scheduler actually checks.

This PR makes the scheduler record where the first stop token would have ended the request, and reports it on every length finish as `meta_info.finish_reason.ignored_stop`.

items.title: [Bugfix] Reap each EngineCore from one thread and kill Ray workers before the monitor join
items.author: AndreasKaratzas
items.summary: Fixes a race condition in CoreEngineProcManager where two threads reap EngineCore processes, causing ECHILD errors, false force-kills, and 4x slower Ray engine shutdown.
items.body:
## Overview

`CoreEngineProcManager` reaps each EngineCore from two threads: the liveness monitor reads `proc.exitcode` (a `waitpid(WNOHANG)`) while `shutdown()` joins the process. When the monitor reaps first, the main thread's `waitpid` gets ECHILD, `Popen.poll()` turns that into "still running", and `shutdown()` logs `force killing remaining process EngineCore` and calls `kill_process_tree()` on a pid that has already been reaped. This makes one thread own reaping. With that fixed, `RayExecutorV2.shutdown()` now kills its actors before joining its monitor thread, so teardown no longer wai

items.title: [Fix] vision: use ViT-scale max-seqlen buckets for flashinfer_cudnn
items.author: Woody-Hu
items.summary: is only consumed by the vision attention backends, but its floor was — an LLM prefill scale. Vision segments are far shorter: - 2x2 window merger in the ViT: 4 tokens per segment - merged tiles (2x2 fold): ~242 tokens - pre-merge tiles: ~1024 tokens rounds the…
items.body:
## Motivation

`FLASHINFER_MAX_SEQLEN_BUCKETS` is only consumed by the vision attention backends (`VisionFlashInferAttention`), but its floor was `4 * 1024` — an LLM prefill scale. Vision segments are far shorter:

- 2x2 window merger in the ViT: **4 tokens** per segment
- merged tiles (2x2 fold): ~242 tokens
- pre-merge tiles: ~1024 tokens

`prepare_flashinfer_cudnn_vision_attention_metadata` rounds the real `max_seqlen` **up** to the next bucket, so every vision segment was padded to 4096 — up to **1024x** over-padding — and cuDNN builds its plan for the padded length, not for the real one.

`_flatten_and_load_videos` opens one decoder per video item and closes them by hand on three exit paths. The Qwen branch never closes them, and the GLM branch closes only on its success returns, so an exception in frame sampling or decoding leaks the decoders and their file handles.

Wrap the body after the decoders are loaded in one `try`/`finally` that closes them, and drop the three explicit closes. The diff is mostly a re-indent; `git diff -w` shows the change. One unit test makes a Qwen decode fail and checks the reader was closed.

## Motivation

Two small fixes in the encoder receiver:

items.title: [Bugfix] Fix None/True/False refcount underflow in stable-ABI C extensions on Python < 3.12
items.author: ist1373
items.summary: Fixes a reference-count underflow of None/True/False in C-extension modules (cumem_allocator, fs_io_C, spinloop) on Python <3.12 that crashes with Fatal Python error: none_dealloc during sleep/wake cycles.
items.body:
## Overview

Fix a refcount underflow of `None`/`True`/`False` in the stable-ABI C extensions (`cumem_allocator`, `fs_io_C`, `spinloop`) on Python 3.11. With sleep mode, each `sleep()`/`wake_up()` drops references to `None` until the interpreter aborts with `Fatal Python error: none_dealloc`.

## Claims

- Fixes `Fatal Python error: none_dealloc: deallocating None` on Python 3.11 with `enable_sleep_mode=True`. It hit an RL colocate training run (in-process engine, sleep/wake every step) after ~1800 steps.
- On a T4 with Qwen2.5-0.5B, main loses 96 references to `None` per `sleep`/`wake_up` c

Fixes #50087.

Under DSPARK speculative decoding, the draft model's block forward borrows `ForwardMode.TARGET_VERIFY` to reuse the verify-style attention metadata and the decode CUDA graph. items.title: [ROCm][Perf][Qwen4Exp] Run dense attention for QSA steps that select every token
items.author: eppaneamd
items.summary: On gfx950 with AITER, a Qwen4Exp QSA step that has a query longer than one token and whose sequences are all at most tokens long (2051 for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) now skips the indexer's scoring and top-k and runs AITER over the paged KV cache. In that range every…
items.body:
## Overview

On gfx950 with AITER, a Qwen4Exp QSA step that has a query longer than one token and whose sequences are all at most `token_topk + compress_ratio - 1` tokens long (2051 for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) now skips the indexer's scoring and top-k and runs AITER `unified_attention` over the paged KV cache. In that range every row's QSA selection is its whole causal prefix, so dense causal attention reads the same tokens. Decode-only steps keep the sparse path and their CUDA graphs. It is the QSA counterpart of sparse MLA's dense-MHA short prefill (#48407, #61942).

## Claims

- Served at TP2

items.author: LuisRobaina

items.body:
## Overview

With prefix caching, the engine sha256-hashes every `prompt_embeds` block on each request.  This PR instead hashes the embeds of a request's new full blocks on a small, lazily created thread pool (`hashlib` releases the GIL), slicing one `memoryview` of the tensor instead of running torch ops per block so the threads don't serialize on the GIL. The digests land in the request's existing per-block cache, so block hashes are byte-identical for every prefix-caching hash algo.

## Claims

At 262k tokens x 4096 bf16: 1.17 s --> 0.22 s
At 262k tokens x 8192 bf16: 2.21 s --> 0.35 s.

items.summary: A vision tower with a smaller head cannot reach it and falls back to. Qwen3-VL uses headdim 72, so that fallback is its default path today. [Discussion: Thank you for contributing to the vLLM project.]
items.body:
## Purpose

aiter's assembly FMHA for gfx950 ships code objects for head_dim **128, 192 and 256 only**. A vision tower with a smaller head cannot reach it and falls back to `ck_tile`. Qwen3-VL uses head_dim 72, so that fallback is its default path today.

Profiling Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B on MI355X:

| path | head_dim at kernel | useful TFLOP/s |
|---|---|---|
| `ck_tile` (current) | 72 native | 409 |
| aiter ASM, head zero-padded | 128 | **1101** |

The padded kernel does `128/72` = **1.78x** the matrix work and is still **2.7x better per useful FLOP**.

Zero-padding is safe: `softmax_scale` stays

items.author: eppaneamd
items.summary: On gfx950 the AMD Qwen4Exp model runs each HyperConnection mix's up projection and as two kernels, so the bf16 gate goes through HBM. This PR adds one Triton kernel that keeps the gate on chip and writes only the mix, used from 256 rows per call.

## Overview

On gfx950 the AMD Qwen4Exp model (`vllm/models/qwen4_exp/amd/`) runs each HyperConnection mix's up projection (`[M, 320] x [320, 10240]`) and `hc_gate_mix` as two kernels, so the `[M, 10240]` bf16 gate goes through HBM. items.title: [ROCm][Perf] Warm the GDN post-conv kernel with the packed b/a layout
items.author: eppaneamd
items.summary: On ROCm, the flat-layout Qwen GDN prefill passes b and a as the two halves of the packed output, but both warm-ups of build them as contiguous tensors. The kernel specializes on the row stride and 16-byte alignment of b and a, so when the value heads per rank …
items.body:
## Overview

On ROCm, the flat-layout Qwen GDN prefill passes `fused_post_conv_prep` b and a as the two halves of the packed `in_proj_ba` output (`ba.chunk(2, dim=-1)`), but both warm-ups of `_fused_post_conv_kernel` build them as contiguous `[L, HV]` tensors. The kernel specializes on the row stride and 16-byte alignment of b and a, so when the value heads per rank are not a multiple of 16 no warmed variant matches a prefill, and a token-count class that no other start-up pass reaches compiles on its first prefill after the server is ready. This PR also warms the packed layout on ROCm.

items.title: [ROCm][JIT] Warm the sparse MLA split-K decode kernels at every split count
items.author: eppaneamd
items.summary: The rope-free sparse MLA decode on ROCm ( with a bf16 or KV cache, e.g. GLM-5.3-Flash) runs a split-K partial and combine kernel pair whose split count is a. [Discussion: Thank you for contributing to the vLLM project.]
items.body:
## Overview

The rope-free sparse MLA decode on ROCm (`ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE` with a bf16 or `mxfp4_mla` KV cache, e.g. GLM-5.3-Flash) runs a split-K partial and combine kernel pair whose split count is a `tl.constexpr`. The count follows the decode batch and its selected KV length, so whenever attention runs outside a FULL CUDA graph, each new count a batch reaches compiles both kernels during serving. This PR registers every count the split heuristic can return when the layer's KV cache is bound, through the decode warm-up hook #65349 added for `TritonMLAImpl`, so the JIT warm-up compiles

items.title: [Perf] qsa: Pass int32 offsets to the sparse kernels on extends
items.author: eppaneamd
items.summary: The extend path builds and, for prefix-hit extends, with, which promotes int32 to int64. HIP decode and the prefill-CP path pass int32 offsets to.
items.body:
## Motivation

The extend path builds `cu_seqlens_q` and, for prefix-hit extends, `cu_seqlens_k` with `cumsum`, which promotes int32 to int64. HIP decode and the prefill-CP path pass int32 offsets to `_sparse_gqa_chunk_prefill`. Triton keys compiled variants on the pointer dtype, so on ROCm the first prefix-hit extend compiled a second variant of a kernel that decode had already compiled for the same row bucket. The kernels widen these offsets to int64 before address arithmetic.

Limits of this PR:
- Measured on MI355X (gfx950) on main's ROCm decode path, which runs `_sparse_gqa_chunk_prefill`

items.title: [Bugfix][NIXL] Don't invalidate a disconnected engine whose agents are gone
items.author: njhill
items.summary: Follow-on to #68047: a pull that fails with now invalidates its remote engine only if the engine still has NIXL agents. Otherwise a disconnect reported after the agents were removed could leave an agent-less engine marked invalid, and would then crash on its.
items.body:
## Overview

Follow-on to #68047: a pull that fails with `NIXL_ERR_REMOTE_DISCONNECT` now invalidates its remote engine only if the engine still has NIXL agents. Otherwise a disconnect reported after the agents were removed could leave an agent-less engine marked invalid, and `_cleanup_remote_engine` would then crash on its `assert engine_id in self._remote_agents`.

## Claims

- A remote disconnect for an engine whose agents were already removed no longer marks that engine invalid, so the cleanup assert can't fire. That matches the metadata-check path, where `all([])` leaves such an engine

## Motivation

With host-only Mamba checkpoints (`SGLANG_OPT_MAMBA_HOST_ONLY_CHECKPOINT`), a checkpoint that was loaded back stays off the device, so a second request can match an anchor whose first load-back is still in flight. `UnifiedRadixCache.init_load_back` then returns `None` for that request, and it retries admission until the first load is acked, even when all it needs is its own Mamba state: the anchor's KV is already on the device (loaded or loading) and nothing of the window pools comes from host.

# [Feat] kv-cache: 4-over-6 block-scale search for the NVFP4 KV cache

## Motivation

The NVFP4 KV cache stores each 16-value block as E2M1 codes with one FP8 block scale, chosen so that the block's largest magnitude maps to 6, the largest E2M1 value. items.body:
## Summary

AITER's custom all-reduce IPC buffer is hardcoded to `8192 * 1024 * 8 * 2` == 128 MiB (`effective_max_size()` returns 64 MiB). For models with large hidden_size and/or large `max_num_batched_tokens`, a full prefill chunk can exceed this cap, falling outside `should_custom_ar`'s runtime guard — the all-reduce then falls back to RCCL instead of the faster custom IPC path, on exactly the chunks that dominate prefill time.

This adds `VLLM_ROCM_AITER_CUSTOM_AR_MAX_SIZE_MB` to override the cap. No change to default behavior — pure opt-in.

## Motivation / evidence

Profiling NemotronH-3

## Purpose

Kimi-K3's `latency_specialized` decode builds FlyDSL kernels at startup for every batch width 1..16 (736 builds, about 51 min on a cold cache). Only widths a FULL decode graph is captured for can run them (FULL replays pad to captured widths; other steps run vLLM's decode), so with the stock ladder only 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16 are ever used. This PR builds only the captured FULL-graph widths <= 16 (`served_widths()`); speculative decode and non-FULL graph modes keep all widths, and FULL graphs with no captured size <= 16 are refused.

## Claims

- Cold start, empty FlyDSL cache, 8x MI355

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash stores its dense linears as `[32, 32]` ue8m0 block FP8. items.body:
`TRTLLM_ENABLE_DUMMY_ALLREDUCE=1` currently inserts profiling synchronization before dispatch and combine in `ExternalCommMoEScheduler`, but neither MegaMoE backend's `FusedCommMoEScheduler` calls `dummy_allreduce()`.

Please support the existing switch in the fused-communication path by bracketing each `backend.run_moe()` with dummy all-reduces. items.title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Report the offending field as error param on validation errors
items.author: hemuku90
items.summary: Fixes Rust frontend returning null param in validation error responses, aligning with Python's behavior of indicating the offending request field.
items.body:
## Overview

Requests rejected by the Rust frontend's derived `validator` checks come back with `"param": null`. Python fills `param` with the offending field for the same requests, and OpenAI clients expose it (`openai.BadRequestError.param`), so callers that branch on it behave differently per frontend.

`ValidatedJson` now reports the field the check failed on. Cross-field checks are collected under `__all__`, so the two Python attributes to a field (`top_logprobs` without `logprobs`, `stream_options` without `stream`) now use a `<field>.<reason>` error code and the field is read from that.

items.title: [Fix] moe: Make biased top-k symbolic-shape safe
items.author: rumitdesai
items.summary: The generic biased TopK implementations fail to trace when the token and expert dimensions are symbolic. For routing scores shaped and a shared correction bias shaped, the intended operation is: The existing implementation reshapes the bias using the symbolic …
items.body:
The generic biased TopK implementations fail to trace when the token and expert dimensions are symbolic.

For routing scores shaped `[T, E]` and a shared correction bias shaped `[E]`, the intended operation is:

```text
[T, E] + [1, E]
```

The existing implementation reshapes the bias using the symbolic expert width:

`correction_bias.view(-1, num_experts)`

When `num_experts` is symbolic, Dynamo represents the inferred leading dimension as `correction_bias.numel() // num_experts`. Fake-tensor tracing cannot always prove that this expression is 1, causing a shape assertion or broadcasting fai

items.title: [Perf] diffusion: Avoid boolean indexing in placeholder validation
items.author: labAxiaoming
items.summary: Boolean indexing adds indexing and gather overhead and can also trigger D2H synchronization on CUDA. Instead, sum the token mask before expand and call.item to retrieve the count.
items.body:
## Motivation

Boolean indexing adds indexing and gather overhead and can also trigger D2H synchronization on CUDA. Instead, sum the token mask before expand and call .item() to retrieve the count. This avoids indexing and gathering while retaining the scalar D2H synchronization.

Count placeholder tokens directly instead. On the reported NVIDIA H800 server, this reduces the isolated counting latency by **15.6–15.7x**. The scalar synchronization from `sum().item()` remains.

## Modifications

- Qwen-VL: replace boolean indexing with `mask[..., 0].sum().item()` for image and video valid

## Problem

Fixes #2532.

slime forwards Megatron's `--save-retain-interval` unchanged, but it saves checkpoint `rollout_id` (0-based): with `--save-interval N` the saved iterations are `N-1, 2N-1, ...`. N-D data-parallel dispatch currently copies each shard to every rank in the model-parallel group. items.author: hiddevandebeek
items.summary: It adds, a KL penalty against the reference policy for. The estimator computes KL(πθ ‖ πref) exactly over the reference top-k tokens plus one tail bucket.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Implements the RFC in #8536. It adds `actor.kl_loss_type: topk_rb`, a KL penalty against the reference policy for `use_kl_loss=True`.

The estimator computes KL(π_θ ‖ π_ref) exactly over the reference top-k tokens plus one tail bucket. The within-tail part is estimated from the sampled token, so the result is an **unbiased** estimate of the full-vocabulary KL gradient at every k, with much lower variance than the single-sample `kl`/`k2`/`low_var_kl`/`k3+` options. It is the per-token Rao-Blackwellised KL of [Amini et al., NeurIPS 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.1063

### What does this PR do?

Preserve vLLM's `finish_reason="length"` in `TokenOutput.stop_reason`. Today the vLLM rollout server reports `completed` both when generation stops naturally and when the output budget cuts it off. A caller translating this value to the Anthropic Messages API consequently sends `end_turn` for a truncated response, and the client can exit with work still in progress.

Map vLLM's `stop` to `completed` and let `length` pass through the existing fallback. Callers can now return `max_tokens` to Anthropic clients. Abort still maps to `aborted`

items.body:
Custom Megatron model providers still need changes to slime's built-in HF loader/exporter registries before they can load a checkpoint and sync weights to rollout engines. This adds two optional import-path callbacks to keep model-specific tensor mappings outside slime:

- `--custom-hf-weight-loader-path`: maps a Megatron parameter/buffer name to its HF tensor. Checkpoint detection honors the callback; loading retains the shared padding, sharding, shape validation and dtype/device copy.
- `--custom-hf-weight-converter-path`: maps a Megatron tensor to HF named tensors after shared normalization

items.title: [reward] fix: compare prime_code call-based outputs as plain builtins
items.author: Aarav500
items.summary: In, call-based tests compared the generated function's return value with. The generated code controls that object, so a subclass of or whose always returns got full reward on every call-based task.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Fixes #8656. In `prime_code`, call-based tests compared the generated function's return value with `output == expected`. The generated code controls that object, so a subclass of `int` or `list` whose `__eq__` always returns `True` got full reward on every call-based task. Swapping the operands doesn't help, because Python tries a subclass's reflected `__eq__` first.

This adds `_to_builtin()` in `prime_code/testing_util.py` and applies it to the output right after the existing `json.dumps(output)` call. It rebuilds the value from plain `None`/`bool`/`int`/`float

items.summary: The engine now owns a device-bound NCCLGroup specialization with a single-device barrier and a logical group key shared across masked/shared ordinal layouts. Allocation, executor-thread broadcast, synchronization and destruction use the engine device.
items.body:
## Problem and behavior

Checkpoint participants each own one GPU, but Ray's default first barrier can enroll every visible GPU and its rendezvous key contains the local ordinal. The engine now owns a device-bound NCCLGroup specialization with a single-device barrier and a logical group key shared across masked/shared ordinal layouts. Allocation, executor-thread broadcast, synchronization and destruction use the engine device. Ordinary Ray groups retain their behavior, and duplicate ownership/topology checks remain. Delta transfers reuse this group and device without changing the wire protocol

items.title: Add `--logits-dtype` to keep Megatron actor logits in bf16
items.author: R0k1e
items.summary: upcasts the last pipeline stage's output to fp32 by default. slime calls the actor with, so the whole logits tensor is copied to fp32.
items.body:
## Motivation

`Float16Module.forward` upcasts the last pipeline stage's output to fp32 by default. slime calls the actor with `labels=None`, so the whole `[T, V]` logits tensor is copied to fp32. The LM head GEMM has already rounded these values to bf16, so the copy adds memory but no precision. It is the largest single allocation in a long-context actor step: 40,960 tokens × 248,320 vocabulary is about 41 GB in fp32 versus 20 GB in bf16.

The fp32 copy does one useful thing: every consumer of the logits computes in fp32 because its input is fp32. This PR keeps that guarantee, but enforces it

Fixes #2515.

`math` and `deepscaler` rewards can get stuck evaluating `9**9**9` or `(10^9)!` against a fractional label. The existing text checks miss Python power notation and large factorial arguments.

Before SymPy evaluates an expression, inspect its token-transformed syntax tree and bound numeric exponent/factorial arguments to 1,000. Numeric estimates use floating-point arithmetic to avoid constructing enormous integers. Symbolic arguments remain supported, including `(n+1)!`, `(2^3)^x`, and small negative powers. items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Allow colocated NPU rollouts to explicitly select vLLM-Ascend's native IPC loading lifecycle. The trainer packs bounded byte buffers, exports a fresh IPC reference for each nonempty bucket, and waits for the worker to finish consuming that bucket. Leaving the option unset preserves the existing CUDA/ROCm, shared-memory and delta dispatch paths.

This is part 1 of a three-PR series: IPC, HCCL, then whole-stream reload.

## Problem

For `k3` and `low_var_kl`, `compute_approx_kl` evaluates `exp(x) - 1 - x`, where `x = log_probs_base - log_probs`. This expression is nonnegative in real arithmetic, but subtracting 1 from a float32 exponential can erase the small KL term or make it negative when the policies are close.

items.body:
## Problem

With `--partial-rollout`, a sample aborted mid-generation goes back to the data buffer and is resumed later. `generate()` resumes it with a `max_new_tokens` budget reduced by `sample.response_length` and appends the new tokens after the existing response, so the request must be conditioned on that response.

For samples with images, the request is built as:

```python
payload["image_data"] = [...]
payload["text"] = sample.prompt
```

`sample.prompt` does not include the response generated so far, so SGLang starts a fresh response from the prompt. The new tokens are then appended af

items.author: 0z5a

items.body:
## Problem

With `--sglang-speculative-algorithm DFLASH` and a colocated rollout engine, the first weight sync silently overwrites the DFLASH draft with target weights. After that, the acceptance length is ~1.0 and rollout is slower than with speculative decoding off.

- slime's colocated sender calls `update_weights_from_tensor` with `serialized_named_tensors`, `load_format="flattened_bucket"` and `weight_version`. It sets neither `selector` nor `disable_draft_model`.

items.title: fix(data): give uniform reward groups exactly zero advantage
items.author: saloni-garg
items.summary: When every rollout in a prompt group gets the same fractional reward, there is no preference between them, so every advantage in the group should be exactly zero. In the group is centered in float32, and for identical rewards that can leave a residue of about …
items.body:
## What does this PR do?

When every rollout in a prompt group gets the same fractional reward, there is no preference between them, so every advantage in the group should be exactly zero. In `_post_process_rewards` the group is centered in float32, and for identical rewards that can leave a residue of about an ulp instead of zero. With std normalization on, the residue is then divided by its own std, which turns it into a small nonzero advantage shared by the whole group.

Small reproduction on current main (a group of 16 rollouts that all scored 0.3, `grpo` with `grpo_std_normalization`):

-
discussion: The nonzero advantages for uniform fractional rewards reproduce on `main`. I ran the grouped-reward tests at `0063710` on CPU with PyTorch 2.13.0: uniform groups produce exact zeros, and the mixed-group and nonfinite-reward cases pass too.
Thank you for checking, and for reproducing it on main as well. Glad the tests hold up on your side too. Happy to run anything else you would like to see here.

items.title: fix(sglang): validate deployment config before launch
items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: Invalid topology or ambiguous model entries could therefore fail late, after router or placement setup had begun.
items.body:
## Background

Multi-model SGLang configuration was resolved incrementally while deployment side effects were already being prepared. Invalid topology or ambiguous model entries could therefore fail late, after router or placement setup had begun.

## Problem

The config path did not validate whole-file invariants such as duplicate model names, multiple weight-updated models, complete engine topology, PP/TP consistency, or multi-node divisibility before launch.

## Solution

- Resolve every model and validate the complete config before placement or router startup.
- Reject unknown model fields

## Background

`RayTrainGroup.create()` allocates training actors sequentially, discovers the rank-0 rendezvous address, initializes every actor, and optionally attaches the rollout manager.

## Problem

A failure at any of those stages left already-created actors alive. Rank 0 was especially vulnerable because it was added to `_actor_handlers` only after its rendezvous lookup succeeded. The non-empty handler list also prevented a clean retry.

## Solution

- Register each actor immediately after creation, before rank-0 rendezvous lookup.

items.title: fix(sglang): bound local server startup waits
items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: A hung health request could block startup indefinitely, and failures while waiting left the newly spawned server process tree running.
items.body:
## Background

Locally managed SGLang servers are polled through `/health_generate` before rollout initialization can continue.

## Problem

The startup poll had neither a request timeout nor an overall deadline. A hung health request could block startup indefinitely, and failures while waiting left the newly spawned server process tree running.

## Solution

- Add `--sglang-server-startup-timeout` with a positive finite value and a conservative 600-second default.
- Use a monotonic deadline and cap every health request by both five seconds and the remaining startup budget.
- Reject readiness

- DeepScaler

## Background

`generate_and_rm_group` supports custom generation that fans one input out into `list[Sample]`, so a fully-async task can return `list[list[Sample]]`.

## Problem

The done callback inspected only the outer list. An aborted leaf inside a fan-out result could therefore enter the completed queue. Requeuing that nested output directly is also invalid because the next generation expects a flat input group.

## Solution

- Snapshot the flat input group before generation can mutate it.
- Inspect one-level fan-out leaves for `Sample.Status.ABORTED`.
- Requeue the pristine flat snapshot

items.title: fix: restore actor weights before initial rollout sync
items.author: tengeel
items.summary: Without, initialization leaves the last auxiliary checkpoint active. Both training entry points synchronize rollout weights before the first training step, so distributed or disk-based synchronization can publish auxiliary weights instead of the resumed actor.
items.body:
## Problem

`MegatronTrainRayActor.init()` backs up the actor and then loads reference, teacher, or old-actor checkpoints into the same model.

Without `--offload-train`, initialization leaves the last auxiliary checkpoint active. Both training entry points synchronize rollout weights before the first training step, so distributed or disk-based synchronization can publish auxiliary weights instead of the resumed actor.

For one resumed run:

| | rollout logprob | reference logprob | actor logprob |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Before | -0.1106 | -0.1111 | -0.1471 |
| After | -0.1088 | -0.1421 | -0.1

Fix CUDA autocast from downcasting the FP32 reduction used by VIME's fused PPO entropy path.

Under CUDA autocast, `torch.einsum` can run at a reduced precision even when both operands were explicitly promoted to FP32. The result is saved for entropy backward, so the precision loss affects both the reported entropy value and its gradient.

This change keeps only that CUDA reduction outside autocast and adds a one-GPU regression suite covering FP16/BF16 autocast, masked/unmasked log-prob paths, metric-only/gradient entropy, and chunked/non-chunked execution.

`distributed_masked_whiten(..., shift_mean=False)` used to center, scale, then add the mean back:

items.author: yuyz-cyber
items.summary: When one task raises an exception, the exception is propagated but the unfinished sibling tasks are not cancelled. They can continue generation or reward computation after the rollout has failed, wasting resources and potentially leaving unobserved task except…
items.body:
## Problem

Training and evaluation launch rollout tasks concurrently at three levels: samples within a rollout group, rollout groups within a training batch, and samples within an evaluation batch.

When one task raises an exception, the exception is propagated but the unfinished sibling tasks are not cancelled. They can continue generation or reward computation after the rollout has failed, wasting resources and potentially leaving unobserved task exceptions in the event loop.

## Fix

At each concurrency boundary, cancel unfinished sibling tasks and wait for their cleanup before re-raising

items.body:
Enabling KL (--kl-coef 0.1 or --use-kl-loss) without --ref-load used to die in slime_validate_args with `TypeError: _path_exists: path should be string, bytes, os.PathLike or integer, not NoneType`, because it stat'd args.ref_load before checking it was set. The sibling OPD check just below already guards for None first.

This adds the same guard: ref_load unset now raises a ValueError telling the user to pass --ref-load, and a ref_load that points nowhere still raises the original FileNotFoundError. Two unit tests cover both cases.

items.body:
## Problem

CI enumerates test files by hand — one `python tests/<file>.py` line per test in `.buildkite/pipeline.yml`, one `(file, num_gpus, ...)` tuple in `.buildkite/gpu_suites.py`. Nothing walks `tests/`, so a test only runs if its author also wired it into a job. Two failure modes, both of which leave CI green:

1. **The file is never wired in.** Three existing files are in this state today and have never run in CI:

   - `tests/test_chunked_gae.py`
   - `tests/test_rollout_metrics.py`

2. **The CPU job's invocation style fails open.**

## Problem

Thanks to @kkyyxhll for catching in #2319 that SGLang ignores `sampling_params.temperature` when it computes input/prefill log-probs. OPD samples from the temperature-scaled student distribution `p_T`, so leaving the teacher at its implicit default computes `KL(p_T || q_1)`, not the matched-temperature objective `KL(p_T || q_T)`.

## Summary
- Expose `--advantage-estimator dapo` as a preset over the existing GRPO implementation.
- Enable Clip-Higher, token-level loss, the default dynamic-sampling filter, and Soft Overlong defaults.
- Add `--soft-overlong-cache` and apply its length penalty before existing reward normalization.
- Document the preset in English and Chinese.

## Design
DAPO does not add a second advantage, loss, or normalization path. Argument validation expands it to the existing GRPO primitives; the only new rollout behavior is Soft Overlong reward shaping.
